issue: Can a federal prisoner invoke the § 2255(e) saving clause to bring a § 2241 challenge when an intervening change in statutory interpretation would make the conviction unlawful and the bar on successive § 2255 motions prevents raising it?

sides.position: The saving clause can be invoked in this situation, so § 2255 is inadequate or ineffective and § 2241 relief is available for a claim based on a change in caselaw combined with the successive-motion bar.
cases: Reyes-Requena v. United States, 243 F.3d 893 (5th Cir. 2001)

sides.position: The saving clause is not available in this situation; being barred from filing a successive § 2255 motion does not make § 2255's remedy inadequate or ineffective.
cases: McCarthan v. Dir. of Goodwill Industries-Suncoast, Inc., 851 F.3d 1076 (11th Cir. 2017) (en banc)

quote: The circuits have split over this question.
cite: Marcus Jones v. Dewayne Hendrix, 8 F.4th 683 (8th Cir. 2021)
